objectives.en: I can use who, which and that to say which person or thing I mean.
objectives.he: אני יודע/ת להשתמש ב-who, ‏which ו-that כדי לומר לאיזה אדם או דבר אני מתכוון/ת.

objectives.en: I can use where for places and whose for possession.
objectives.he: אני יודע/ת להשתמש ב-where למקומות וב-whose לשייכות.

objectives.en: I can leave out who/which/that when it is the object, and I don't repeat the pronoun: the book I read, not *the book that I read it.
objectives.he: אני יודע/ת להשמיט את who/which/that כשהם המושא, ולא לחזור על הכינוי: the book I read, ולא the book that I read it.

warmup.en: How would you explain the words 'dentist' and 'library' to someone who doesn't know them? Try: 'It's a person who...' and 'It's a place where...'
warmup.he: איך הייתם מסבירים את המילים dentist ו-library למישהו שלא מכיר אותן? נסו: "It's a person who..." ו-"It's a place where..."

explanation.en: Look: A dentist is a person who looks after your teeth. A library is a place where you can borrow books. That's the phone that I want. A relative clause comes right after a noun and tells us which person, thing or place we mean.
explanation.he: שימו לב: A dentist is a person who looks after your teeth. ‏A library is a place where you can borrow books. ‏That's the phone that I want. משפט זיקה (relative clause) בא מיד אחרי שם עצם ומסביר לאיזה אדם, דבר או מקום מתכוונים – בדומה ל-"ש..." בעברית.

rows: The woman who lives next door is a nurse.
The bus which goes to the airport leaves every hour.
people or things (very common in speech)
The film that we saw was great.
That's the café where we met.
I have a friend whose brother is a chef.

explanation.en: If who/which/that is the subject of the clause (a verb comes next), keep it: the man who called you. If it is the object (a new subject comes next), you can leave it out: the film (that) we saw, the people (who) I met.
explanation.he: אם who/which/that הם הנושא של משפט הזיקה (מיד אחריהם בא פועל), חייבים להשאיר אותם: the man who called you. אם הם המושא (אחריהם בא נושא חדש), אפשר להשמיט אותם: the film (that) we saw, the people (who) I met.

explanation.en: The relative word already stands for the noun, so don't repeat it as a pronoun: the book (that) I read (not *the book that I read it); the friend (who) I live with (not *the friend that I live with her). Hebrew often repeats the pronoun (literally 'the book that I read it'), but English never does.
explanation.he: מילת הזיקה כבר מחליפה את שם העצם, ולכן לא חוזרים עליו בכינוי: the book (that) I read (ולא the book that I read it); ‏the friend (who) I live with (ולא the friend that I live with her). בעברית חוזרים לעיתים קרובות על הכינוי ("הספר שקראתי אותו", "החברה שאני גר/ה איתה"), אבל באנגלית אף פעם לא.

explanation.en: whose = possession; who's = who is. They sound the same: /huːz/. Use where only when a subject + verb follows: the café where we met, but a café that sells great cakes. These clauses tell us which one we mean, so they have no commas.
explanation.he: whose = שייכות; ‏who's = who is. הן נשמעות אותו דבר: /huːz/. משתמשים ב-where רק כשאחריו בא נושא + פועל: the café where we met, אבל a café that sells great cakes. המשפטים האלה מגדירים לאיזה דבר מתכוונים, ולכן אין לפניהם פסיק.

examples.en: A pharmacist is someone who prepares and sells medicines.
examples.he: רוקח/ת הוא מי שמכין ומוכר תרופות.

hebrew_pitfalls.en: In Hebrew a relative clause often repeats the noun as a pronoun (literally 'the book that I read it', 'the friend that I live with her'). In English the relative word already does that job, so don't add it, him, her or them: the book (that) I read; the friend (who) I live with.
hebrew_pitfalls.he: בעברית משפט זיקה חוזר לעיתים קרובות על שם העצם בכינוי ("הספר שקראתי אותו", "החברה שאני גר/ה איתה"). באנגלית מילת הזיקה כבר עושה את העבודה הזאת, ולכן לא מוסיפים it, ‏him, ‏her או them: the book (that) I read; ‏the friend (who) I live with.

hebrew_pitfalls.en: /w/ is not a regular Hebrew sound (it appears mainly in borrowed words), so which, where and we can come out with a v: 'vich', 'vere'. For /w/, round your lips as for 'oo' and keep your teeth away from your lip: which /wɪtʃ/, where /weə(r)/.
hebrew_pitfalls.he: ‏/w/ אינו צליל רגיל בעברית (הוא מופיע בעיקר במילים שאולות), ולכן which, ‏where ו-we עלולים להישמע עם v. כדי להגות /w/ עגלו את השפתיים כמו ב-"או", ואל תגעו בשיניים בשפה: which /wɪtʃ/, ‏where /weə(r)/.

prompt.en: Match each word with its definition.

pairs: a person who looks after your teeth
a place where you can borrow books

explanation.en: a person who..., a place where..., a thing that... – the easiest way to explain a word you don't know in English.
explanation.he: a person who..., ‏a place where..., ‏a thing that... – הדרך הקלה ביותר להסביר באנגלית מילה שאתם לא מכירים.

prompt.en: Which word completes each phrase: who, which, where or whose?
prompt.he: איזו מילה משלימה כל צירוף: who, ‏which, ‏where או whose?

items.text: the app ___ I use for music
the bag ___ was on the table

explanation.en: who = people; which = things; where = places + subject + verb (we stayed, I was born); whose = possession (his bike, her songs). Note: the hotel which we stayed is wrong – you'd need 'in': the hotel which we stayed in.
explanation.he: who = אנשים; ‏which = דברים; ‏where = מקומות + נושא + פועל (we stayed, I was born); ‏whose = שייכות (האופניים שלו, השירים שלה). שימו לב: the hotel which we stayed שגוי – צריך in: ‏the hotel which we stayed in.

exercises.question: That's the man ___ car was stolen.
options: who
whose
who's
which

0.en: who can't show possession. His car → whose car.
0.he: who לא מבטא שייכות. "המכונית שלו" = whose car.

2.en: who's = who is: *the man who is car... doesn't make sense. For possession, use whose.
2.he: who's = who is, וזה לא מתאים כאן. לשייכות משתמשים ב-whose.

3.en: which is for things, and it doesn't show possession here. Use whose.
3.he: which משמש לדברים, והוא לא מבטא כאן שייכות. השתמשו ב-whose.

explanation.en: whose = his/her/their: the man whose car was stolen = the man; his car was stolen.
explanation.he: whose = שלו/שלה/שלהם: the man whose car was stolen = האיש שהמכונית שלו נגנבה.

exercises.question: Is this the bus ___ goes to the station?
options: where
who
what
that

0.en: A verb (goes) comes next, so you need a subject word: that or which. Use where only before a subject + verb: the stop where we wait.
0.he: מיד אחרי בא פועל (goes), ולכן צריך מילה שהיא נושא: that או which. ‏where בא רק לפני נושא + פועל: the stop where we wait.

1.en: who is for people, not buses.

2.en: what can't start a relative clause: the bus that (or which) goes...
2.he: what לא פותח משפט זיקה: the bus that (או which) goes...

explanation.en: A thing + subject relative: that or which. the bus that goes = the bus; it goes.
explanation.he: דבר + מילת זיקה שהיא הנושא: that או which. ‏the bus that goes = האוטובוס שנוסע.

exercises.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The book I read was really good.
The book that I read it was really good.
The book I read it was really good.
The book what I read was really good.

1.en: Don't repeat the book as it: that already stands for it.
1.he: לא חוזרים על the book בעזרת it: ‏that כבר מחליף אותו.

2.en: The pronoun it repeats the book. Drop it: The book I read was really good.
2.he: הכינוי it חוזר על the book. מוחקים אותו: The book I read was really good.

3.en: what can't start a relative clause: the book (that) I read.
3.he: what לא פותח משפט זיקה: the book (that) I read.

explanation.en: the book (that) I read: that is the object, so you can leave it out – but you never add it at the end.
explanation.he: the book (that) I read: ‏that הוא המושא, ולכן אפשר להשמיט אותו – אבל אף פעם לא מוסיפים it בסוף.

wrong_feedback.match: who's

feedback.en: who's = who is. For possession (her name), use whose.
feedback.he: who's = who is. לשייכות (השם שלה) משתמשים ב-whose.

wrong_feedback.match: what

feedback.en: what can't start a relative clause. Use who, which, that, where or whose.
feedback.he: what לא פותח משפט זיקה. השתמשו ב-who, ‏which, ‏that, ‏where או whose.

wrong_feedback.match: which

feedback.en: which is for things as subject or object. Use where for a place + subject + verb (I grew up), whose for possession, and who for people.
feedback.he: which משמש לדברים. ‏where בא לפני נושא + פועל במקום (I grew up), ‏whose לשייכות, ו-who לאנשים.

wrong_feedback.match: who

feedback.en: who is for people (a teacher who played...). Use whose for possession (a girl whose name) and that/which for things (a school that had).
feedback.he: who משמש לאנשים (a teacher who played...). ‏whose לשייכות (a girl whose name), ו-that/which לדברים (a school that had).

wrong_feedback.match: that

feedback.en: that works for people and things, but not before a place + subject + verb (use where: the city where I grew up) or for possession (use whose).
feedback.he: that מתאים לאנשים ולדברים, אבל לא לפני נושא + פועל במקום (משתמשים ב-where: the city where I grew up) ולא לשייכות (משתמשים ב-whose).

wrong_feedback.match: where

feedback.en: where needs a subject + verb after it. Before a verb (had, played), use that, which or who.
feedback.he: אחרי where צריך לבוא נושא + פועל. לפני פועל (had, played) משתמשים ב-that, ‏which או who.

hint.en: Place + subject + verb → where. Possession → whose.
hint.he: מקום + נושא + פועל = where. שייכות = whose.

explanation.en: the city where I grew up (place + subject + verb); a girl whose name (= her name); a school that/which had (thing, subject); a teacher who/that played (person, subject).
explanation.he: the city where I grew up (מקום + נושא + פועל); ‏a girl whose name (= השם שלה); ‏a school that/which had (דבר, נושא); ‏a teacher who/that played (אדם, נושא).

feedback.en: Hebrew repeats the pronoun (literally 'that I lived in it'), but in English which already means 'it': the flat which I lived in.
feedback.he: בעברית חוזרים על הכינוי ("שגרתי בה"), אבל באנגלית which כבר מחליף אותו: the flat which I lived in.

wrong_feedback.match: This is the apartment I lived in it last year.

feedback.en: Drop it: the flat I lived in. English doesn't repeat the noun as a pronoun.
feedback.he: מוחקים את it: ‏the flat I lived in. באנגלית לא חוזרים על שם העצם בכינוי.

wrong_feedback.match: This is the apartment where I lived in last year.

feedback.en: where already includes "in". Write the flat where I lived, or the flat (that) I lived in.
feedback.he: where כבר כולל את "in". כתבו the flat where I lived או the flat (that) I lived in.

wrong_feedback.match: This is the apartment that I lived last year.

feedback.en: live needs in: the flat (that) I lived in – or use where: the flat where I lived.
feedback.he: אחרי live צריך in: ‏the flat (that) I lived in – או where: ‏the flat where I lived.

wrong_feedback.match: This is the apartment I lived last year.

feedback.en: live needs in: the flat I lived in – or use where: the flat where I lived.
feedback.he: אחרי live צריך in: ‏the flat I lived in – או where: ‏the flat where I lived.

hint.en: Two correct patterns: 'where I lived' or '(that) I lived in'.
hint.he: שתי דרכים נכונות: "where I lived" או "(that) I lived in".

explanation.en: Hebrew says 'that I lived in it'. English either uses where (where I lived) or puts in at the end with no pronoun ((that) I lived in).
explanation.he: בעברית אומרים "שגרתי בה". באנגלית משתמשים ב-where ‏(where I lived), או שמים את in בסוף בלי כינוי ‏((that) I lived in).

prompt.en: Read Lior's blog post and answer the questions.
prompt.he: קראו את הפוסט של ליאור בבלוג וענו על השאלות.

exercises.title: Lior's blog: The people who make my street special
exercises.passage:
I've lived on Herzl Street for six years, and I think it's the best street in the city. It isn't because of the buildings – they're old and a bit ugly. It's because of the people who live and work here.

First, there's Mrs Avraham, the woman who runs the tiny kiosk on the corner. She knows everyone's name, and she always remembers the newspaper that you like.

Next to the kiosk there's a bike shop whose owner, Kenji, moved here from Japan ten years ago. He's the person I call when anything breaks – not just bikes. Last month he fixed a radio that belonged to my grandmother, and he didn't even ask for money.

Across the road there's a café where students sit for hours with their laptops. The coffee isn't amazing, but the cakes that Rana bakes every morning are the best I've ever eaten.

And then there's the man upstairs who plays the trumpet. He's the only person on the street that nobody really likes – at least not at seven o'clock on a Saturday morning!

What about your street? Who are the people who make it special?

– Lior

questions.question: Who is Kenji?
options: the man who runs the kiosk
the owner of the bike shop
the man who plays the trumpet

0.en: The kiosk is run by Mrs Avraham.

2.en: The trumpet player is the man upstairs. His name isn't given.
2.he: נגן החצוצרה הוא השכן מלמעלה. השם שלו לא מופיע.

explanation.en: 'a bike shop whose owner, Kenji, moved here from Japan' – whose owner = the shop's owner.
explanation.he: בטקסט: a bike shop whose owner, Kenji, moved here from Japan. ‏whose owner = הבעלים של החנות.

questions.statement: Mrs Avraham remembers which newspaper each customer likes.

explanation.en: 'She always remembers the newspaper that you like.'
explanation.he: בטקסט: She always remembers the newspaper that you like.

questions.statement: Lior thinks the café's coffee is excellent.

explanation.en: 'The coffee isn't amazing' – it's the cakes that are excellent.
explanation.he: בטקסט: The coffee isn't amazing – העוגות הן שמצוינות.

questions.question: What did Kenji fix last month?
options: a radio that belonged to Lior's grandmother
Lior's bike
the café's coffee machine

1.en: Kenji fixes bikes, but last month he fixed something else: a radio.
1.he: קנג'י מתקן אופניים, אבל בחודש שעבר הוא תיקן משהו אחר: רדיו.

2.en: The text doesn't mention a coffee machine.
2.he: בטקסט אין אזכור של מכונת קפה.

explanation.en: 'Last month he fixed a radio that belonged to my grandmother.'
explanation.he: בטקסט: Last month he fixed a radio that belonged to my grandmother.

questions.text: The cakes that ___ bakes every morning are the best Lior has ever eaten.
answers: Rana

explanation.en: 'the cakes that Rana bakes every morning' – that is the object, Rana is the subject.
explanation.he: בטקסט: the cakes that Rana bakes every morning. ‏that הוא המושא, ורנא היא הנושא.

questions.statement: Everyone on the street likes the trumpet player.

explanation.en: 'He's the only person on the street that nobody really likes.'
explanation.he: בטקסט: He's the only person on the street that nobody really likes.

explanation.en: Notice how relative clauses identify each person and place: the woman who runs..., a bike shop whose owner..., a café where...
explanation.he: שימו לב איך משפטי הזיקה מזהים כל אדם ומקום: the woman who runs..., ‏a bike shop whose owner..., ‏a café where...

exercises.audio_text: The woman who lives next door has a dog that never stops barking.
answers: The woman who lives next door has a dog that never stops barking.
The woman who lives next door has a dog which never stops barking.

explanation.en: Two relative clauses: who lives next door (a person), that never stops barking (an animal). Both are subjects, so they must stay.
explanation.he: שני משפטי זיקה: who lives next door (אדם), ‏that never stops barking (בעל חיים). בשניהם מילת הזיקה היא הנושא, ולכן חייבים להשאיר אותה.

prompt.en: You're showing a friend around your town. Say this out loud.
prompt.he: אתם עושים לחבר סיור בעיר שלכם. אמרו את זה בקול.

exercises.target: That's the café where we usually meet.

focus.en: where and we start with /w/: round your lips as for 'oo', and keep your teeth away from your lip – not 'vere', 'vee'.
focus.he: where ו-we מתחילים ב-/w/: עגלו את השפתיים כמו ב-"או" ואל תגעו בשיניים בשפה – לא "vere" ולא "vee".

explanation.en: a place + where + subject + verb: the café where we usually meet.
explanation.he: מקום + where + נושא + פועל: the café where we usually meet.

prompt.en: Write a short blog post about a place you know well.
prompt.he: כתבו פוסט קצר בבלוג על מקום שאתם מכירים היטב.

task.en: Write a blog post (80-120 words) about a street, neighbourhood or place you know well and the people in it. Use at least five relative clauses with who, which/that, where and whose. Leave out the relative word at least once where you can (the café I love).
task.he: כתבו פוסט בבלוג (80-120 מילים) על רחוב, שכונה או מקום שאתם מכירים היטב ועל האנשים שבו. השתמשו לפחות בחמישה משפטי זיקה עם who, ‏which/that, ‏where ו-whose. השמיטו את מילת הזיקה לפחות פעם אחת במקום שאפשר (the café I love).

exercises.model_answer: My favourite place is the small market in my neighbourhood, where my family shops every Friday. There's a fruit seller who always gives me a free orange, and a bakery whose challah is the best in town. My favourite stall is the one that sells spices from all over the world. The man who runs it is called Eli, and he loves telling stories about the places he has visited. There's also a tiny café I go to after school. The people who work there know exactly what I want before I order. It's a place where I always feel at home.

checklist.en: I used at least five relative clauses: who (people), which/that (things), where (places), whose (possession).
checklist.he: השתמשתי לפחות בחמישה משפטי זיקה: who (אנשים), ‏which/that (דברים), ‏where (מקומות), ‏whose (שייכות).

checklist.en: I didn't repeat the noun as a pronoun (not *the café that I love it).
checklist.he: לא חזרתי על שם העצם בכינוי (ולא the café that I love it).

checklist.en: I left out the relative word only when a new subject follows (the café I go to), never before a verb.
checklist.he: השמטתי את מילת הזיקה רק כשאחריה בא נושא חדש (the café I go to), אף פעם לא לפני פועל.

checklist.en: I used whose (not who's) for possession.

explanation.en: Relative clauses let you describe people and places precisely in one sentence instead of two.
explanation.he: משפטי זיקה מאפשרים לתאר אנשים ומקומות בדיוק, במשפט אחד במקום שניים.

key_points.en: who = people, which = things, that = both, where = places (+ subject + verb), whose = possession.
key_points.he: who = אנשים, ‏which = דברים, ‏that = שניהם, ‏where = מקומות (+ נושא + פועל), ‏whose = שייכות.

key_points.en: Don't repeat the noun as a pronoun: the book (that) I read, not *the book that I read it.
key_points.he: לא חוזרים על שם העצם בכינוי: the book (that) I read, ולא the book that I read it.

key_points.en: You can leave out who/which/that when a new subject follows (the film we saw), but not before a verb (the man who called).
key_points.he: אפשר להשמיט את who/which/that כשאחריהם בא נושא חדש (the film we saw), אבל לא לפני פועל (the man who called).

key_points.en: With a preposition: the flat where I lived = the flat (that) I lived in.
key_points.he: עם מילת יחס: the flat where I lived = the flat (that) I lived in.
